title: Dividing a Unit Fraction by a Whole Number

blocks.html: You can multiply fractions, and division is fair sharing. What happens when the thing being shared is itself a fraction, like $\frac{1}{3}$ of a pan of cornbread?
$\frac{1}{a} \div b = \frac{1}{a \times b}$. Sharing $\frac{1}{3}$ among 4 people gives each $\frac{1}{12}$. Check with multiplication: $\frac{1}{12} \times 4 = \frac{1}{3}$.

Cut the $\frac{1}{3}$ into 4 equal pieces. If you did that to every third of the pan, the whole pan would be cut into $3 \times 4 = 12$ pieces of the same size. So each share is $\frac{1}{12}$ of the pan. Dividing by 4 is the same as taking $\frac{1}{4}$ of it: $\frac{1}{4} \times \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{12}$.

blocks.name: fractionbar
blocks.cap: $\frac{1}{3}$ of the bar is the same as 4 twelfths. One of those 4 equal shares is $\frac{1}{12}$.

blocks.title: Share a third
steps: The whole would have $3 \times 4 = 12$ such parts, so each is $\frac{1}{12}$.

blocks.title: A story
blocks.q: Five friends share $\frac{1}{2}$ pound of trail mix equally. How much does each get?

blocks.html: Answering with a bigger fraction, such as $\frac{1}{3} \div 4 = \frac{4}{3}$. Sharing makes each part smaller than what was shared. Check by multiplying back: $\frac{4}{3} \times 4$ is far more than $\frac{1}{3}$.
